tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 5; NIST TN 1822 Verif.1.1 (IMO Test 5)
tests.name: pre-movement uniform 10 to 100 s, ten persons in an 8 m x 5 m room
tests.criterion: each starts at an appropriate time: first moves within [10, 100] s, and uniform (KS p > 0.05)
tests.summary: first moves 11 to 99.2 s, KS p 0.775 (crowd.js 'start' is a stagger; the performance check models pre-movement)

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.1.1 (a modified IMO Test 5)
tests.name: pre-evacuation times of ten persons in an 8 m x 5 m room, for each distribution the model takes, the alarm at 30 s
tests.criterion: no one moves before the time drawn for them, the first moves after the alarm lie within the distribution's range and follow it (KS p > 0.05; 30 runs of ten persons)

measured.distribution: log-normal, median 60 s, sigma 0.5, cut off at 30 and 150 s
normal, mean 60 s, sd 20 s, cut off at 20 and 100 s

tests.summary: uniform 10 to 100 s: 10.66 to 99.93 s (median 54.25), KS p 0.848; log-normal, median 60 s, sigma 0.5: 13.28 to 208.49 s (median 57.76), KS p 0.386; log-normal, median 60 s, sigma 0.5, cut off at 30 and 150 s: 30.17 to 143.45 s (median 59.96), KS p 0.543; normal, mean 60 s, sd 20 s, cut off at 20 and 100 s: 21.72 to 98.45 s (median 58.48), KS p 0.356; Weibull, scale 60 s, shape 1.5: 2.26 to 222.82 s (median 46.24), KS p 0.848; 2 of 1500 first moves held up behind someone, by 0.371 s at most
tests.deviation: a person whose way is taken at the time drawn for them moves when it clears: the first move is then later than the time drawn

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.2.5 (after Korhonen and Hostikka 2009)
tests.name: one occupant at 1.25 m/s along a 2 m x 100 m corridor, clear and at an extinction coefficient of 1.0 /m
tests.criterion: the time in smoke within 1 % of the hand calculation by the model's relation, v = v0 max(0.1, 1 + beta K / alpha), alpha 0.706 m/s, beta -0.057 m2/s (FDS+Evac's, after Frantzich and Nilsson); the clear time that at 1.25 m/s
tests.summary: 100.5 m in 87.46 s in smoke (hand calculation 87.46 s), 1.1491 m/s against the relation's 1.1491; clear 80.4 s
tests.deviation: the exit is one door node at the corridor's end, 100.5 m from the start; the smoke is given as a visibility of 3 / K in every place

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.2.5, user actions (the speeds and coefficients of the two data sets)
tests.name: the same corridor at 1.25, 1.0, 0.75, 0.5 and 0.25 m/s and extinction coefficients of 0.5, 1.0, 3.0, 7.5 and 10 /m
tests.criterion: each speed within 1 % of FDS+Evac's relation: v0 max(0.1, 1 + beta K / alpha)
tests.summary: 25 of 25 at FDS+Evac's relation, the slowest walkers in the thickest smoke included

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 7; NIST TN 1822 Verif.2.4 (IMO Test 7)
tests.name: 50 persons' unimpeded speeds against the distribution assigned (uniform 0.89 to 1.49 m/s)
tests.criterion: speeds consistent with the distribution assigned (KS p > 0.05)
tests.summary: moving 0.895 to 1.484 m/s (median 1.207) against 0.893 to 1.487; KS p 0.2841
tests.deviation: crowd.js assigns a uniform spread about one speed; RiMEA's population (Weidmann's speeds by age) cannot be set

tests.name: 400 persons of the Weidmann population (normal, mean 1.34 m/s, sd 0.26, cut off at 0.6 and 2.0)
tests.criterion: unimpeded speeds consistent with the population assigned (KS p > 0.05)
tests.summary: moving 0.672 to 1.968 m/s (median 1.35); KS p 0.8304

tests.name: 400 males of 30 to 50 years (uniform 0.97 to 1.62 m/s)
tests.criterion: unimpeded speeds consistent with the population assigned (KS p > 0.05)
tests.summary: moving 0.971 to 1.619 m/s (median 1.295); KS p 0.3613

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.5.2 (IMO Test 4; MSC/Circ.1238's 1.33 persons/s/m)
tests.name: 100 persons through a 1 m exit: the flow never above 1.33 persons/s
tests.criterion: flow at the exit over the whole period, and in any 10 s, at most 1.33 persons/s
tests.summary: mean 0.923 persons/s, peak 10 s 0.9 (the door's SFPE capacity 0.921)

tests.name: an exit closing at 10 s
tests.criterion: no one steps out by it after it closes; everyone still leaves
tests.summary: 0 steps on to the closed exit begun after 10 s (2 begun before it closed, ending after); 240 of 240 out

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.3.1 (IMO Test 10); RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 10
tests.name: exit choice in a corridor with twelve rooms, a main and a secondary exit
tests.criterion: a deterministic model sends everyone to the closest exit (NIST); RiMEA's assignment by room cannot be set in crowd.js
tests.summary: nearest: 115 of 115 to their closest exit; 79 of 91 in rooms where RiMEA assigns them; quickest used main 61, secondary 54
tests.deviation: persons start at random over rooms, corridor and passage, and choose their own exit

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 10; NIST TN 1822 Verif.3.1 (IMO Test 10)
tests.name: 23 persons in twelve rooms, each room given the main or the secondary exit
tests.criterion: everyone leaves by the exit given to them

measured.placing: two persons a room, one in room 3, as IMO's figure has them

tests.summary: 115 of 115 left by the exit given to them (main 75, secondary 40)

tests.name: room 1's evacuation against the goal's distance a past the bottleneck (0.5 to 10 m)
tests.criterion: the time rises with a until it is constant (documentation)
tests.deviation: about 150 start in room 1 (persons start at random over both rooms; those who start in room 2 are left out of the reading)

tests.name: a 5 m long, 1 m wide bottleneck against a short one
tests.criterion: room 1 takes longer to empty through the long bottleneck
tests.summary: short (one door node) 163.3 s; long corridor 196.6 s; long with door nodes at its ends 194.4 s
tests.deviation: the long bottleneck is two lattice rows (z 5 and 5.5 m); a corridor carries no door capacity in crowd.js, only one person a node

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 12d (Fig. 15, flows from experiments: Kretz et al. 2006; Seyfried et al. 2009; about 1.9 w persons/s)
tests.name: flow through a bottleneck 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 m wide
tests.criterion: the flow rises with the width (verification); and, as validation, how near it is to the measured flows
tests.summary: 0.8 m: 0.658 persons/s (SFPE 0.658, measured about 1.52); 1 m: 0.921 persons/s (SFPE 0.921, measured about 1.9); 1.2 m: 1.184 persons/s (SFPE 1.184, measured about 2.28)
tests.validation: fails as a match to the measured flows by design: the SFPE capacity is a design value, about half the laboratory flows

tests.name: 150 persons through three rooms joined by two identical bottlenecks 1 m wide
tests.criterion: the numbers in rooms 1 and 2 over time and the flows through bottlenecks 1 and 2 (documentation: the test gives an aim, no expected result)
tests.summary: bottleneck 1 0.921 persons/s, bottleneck 2 0.917; at most 12 in room 2 at once; longest wait before bottleneck 2 0.743 s
tests.deviation: the rooms are taken as 10 m x 10 m, as Test 12b's (Fig. 14's dimensions were not read); the bottlenecks are short (one door node each); the default population, not RiMEA's

tests.source: SFPE Handbook, 5th ed., ch. 59 (specific flow and boundary layers); the values Pathfinder's SFPE mode reports (Thunderhead Engineering, Verification and Validation)
tests.name: what a door, a corridor and a stair 1 m wide pass, and a stair against its width
tests.criterion: 150 persons queueing: the flows within 5 % of 0.92 (door), 0.79 (corridor) and 0.71 persons/s (stair, down), and a wider stair passes more
tests.summary: 1 m door 0.921, corridor 0.789, stair 0.705 persons/s (SFPE 0.92, 0.79, 0.71); stairs down 1 m: 0.705 (SFPE 0.71; up 0.528), 1.2 m: 0.913 (SFPE 0.913; up 0.685), 2.4 m: 2.13 (SFPE 2.131; up 1.597); 1 m stair with a node a tread: 0.676
tests.deviation: the stair is a single file of nodes 0.5 m apart carrying its width (graph.widths), as the app draws a stair, with a wide exit (5 m) at its far end; with a node a tread (0.33 m) the 1 m stair is reported beside the criterion, not in it; the corridor is two lattice rows

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.5.1 (modified IMO Test 11: the stair leads down)
tests.name: congestion: 100 persons in an 8 m x 5 m room, a corridor 2 m wide and 12 m long, a stair down at its end
tests.criterion: qualitative, read here as: congestion before the room's exit (mean density above SFPE's greatest-flow density, 1.9 persons/m2, while the room empties), a steady flow in the corridor (its middle never above that density; the flow past it in 5 s bins varying by at most a quarter), and congestion at the base of the stair (peak density above 1.9; the stair takes less than the corridor brings)
tests.summary: density before the room's exit 3.827/m2; corridor middle peak 1.444/m2, flow 1.957 persons/s (variation 0.073); stair base peak 2.333/m2, on to the stair 1.707 persons/s; last out 80.667 s
tests.deviation: the stair is taken as 2 m wide, as the corridor (the figure's stair dimension was not read), 5 m along the slope, and is a single file of nodes carrying its width, with a wide exit (5 m) at its foot; the room opens on the corridor over its full width; the default population (1.19 m/s, 25 % either way)

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 16 (percentiles: rimea.de test_16_percentiles.xlsx; raw data Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.8378592)
tests.name: single-file fundamental diagram, 200 m corridor one agent wide
tests.criterion: mean speeds between the experiments' 10 and 90 % percentiles at the measured density (validation)
tests.deviation: the lattice holds at most 2 persons/m in single file (0.5 m nodes); measured in x 40 to 80 m between 10 and 40 s, before the exit's queue reaches it

tests.name: fundamental diagram in a 10 m wide corridor (2 m x 2 m measuring area)
tests.criterion: documentation: speed against density beside the model's SFPE relation and Weidmann's
tests.deviation: 100 m long, not 1,000 m; the lattice holds at most 4 persons/m2 (RiMEA asks up to 6); measured between 10 and 40 s

tests.name: 1,000 persons leave a hall by four doors, then by two
tests.criterion: about twice the time with two doors (documentation, not an exclusion criterion: footnote 8)
tests.summary: four doors 274.1 s, two 544.7 s: 1.99 times
tests.deviation: persons spread over the whole hall rather than the 26 m x 16 m area; walking speeds crowd.js's uniform spread, not RiMEA's population

tests.name: 1,000 persons, two exits 5 m apart in one wall
tests.criterion: most prefer the closer exit 1, congestion there, some use exit 2
tests.summary: quickest: 50.2 % by exit 1 (longest wait 527.9 s); nearest: 59.3 %
tests.deviation: persons spread over the whole room, not packed from the left side (crowd.js has no start areas), so exit 2 is the nearer for those far right

tests.name: 1,000 adults packed from the left side, two exits 5 m apart in one wall
tests.criterion: the persons prefer the closer exit 1, congestion occurs there, and some use exit 2

measured.speeds: Weidmann's normal population (RiMEA gives its speeds by age as a curve only)

tests.summary: 50.5 % by exit 1 (longest wait 529.8 s), the rest by exit 2

tests.name: one occupant at 1 m/s in a 10 m x 15 m room, Exit 1 unavailable after 1 s
tests.criterion: Exit 1 is not used by the occupant
tests.summary: right of centre: Exit 2 (both open: Exit 2); left of centre, nearer Exit 1: Exit 2 (both open: Exit 1)
